name: Third Cinema
summary: A militant film that works as a tool, not as a show. It uses a light 16mm camera, black and white stock, real streets and factories, archive clips, slogans on screen and direct address. The picture is rough and the cut is an argument.

philosophy.core_thesis: A film made outside the studio and outside the art house is a weapon for a people in a struggle, so each image must serve an argument and each screening must start a debate.
design_principles: Shoot with a light 16mm camera and a crew of 2 to 6 people, in the streets, the factories and the villages.
Cast real workers and activists as themselves, and let them speak to the camera.
Cut live footage against newsreel, photographs, statistics and printed slogans, to make a claim.
Split the film into chapters with title cards of 2 to 6 words and a clear question.
Use handheld takes of 5 to 20 s and a hard cut, and hold a face when it speaks.
Lay a voice-over or a song over the image, and leave gaps for the audience to answer.
Show the film in a meeting room or a union hall, and stop it for a debate.
anti_patterns: A studio set or a star actor
A score that decorates the image
A scene that entertains and makes no claim
A neutral voice that hides the maker's side
A tidy ending that closes the argument

composition.framing: A tight, plain 4:3 or 1.37:1 frame at eye level; faces fill the frame in an interview, and a crowd fills it in a march.
composition.staging_in_depth: 2 planes: a speaker in front and a wall, a poster or a crowd behind, as found.
composition.subject_placement: Centre a speaker who looks at the lens; place a crowd or a machine off centre.

principles.rule: Frame a speaker close and let the eyes meet the lens.
Put the printed slogan or the face on the centre line.
principles.value: title cards of 2 to 6 words, centred

principles.rule: Keep the street or the factory visible behind the speaker.
Use daylight and the lamps in the room.
principles.value: 0 added lamps, 3:1 or lower key to fill

principles.rule: Cut a long talk against a short burst of archive images.
principles.value: 3 to 6 s average shot, with takes up to 60 s

camera_and_movement.movement: A handheld follow of a march or a worker, a zoom to a face, and a static take for a speech.
camera_and_movement.support: Handheld or shoulder-braced 16mm camera; a tripod for a talk
camera_and_movement.move_speed: Walking pace 1.0 to 1.6 m/s; a zoom over 1 to 4 s

lens_and_format.focal_length: a 10mm to 16mm wide lens for a crowd, a 25mm to 75mm zoom for a face
lens_and_format.aperture: f/2.8 to f/8, set by the available light
lens_and_format.focus: Hand-set focus on the main face, with a slip allowed when the camera moves
equipment: a portable tape recorder or a sync sound unit
a fast black and white stock
a slide projector for copy shots

light.quality: Hard daylight, a bare room lamp and a window; a flat, contrasty black and white image.
light.direction: From a window, the sky or a lamp in the room.
light.colour_temperature: Not set; the film is black and white
light.source: The sun, windows, street lamps and bare bulbs

colour_and_grade.treatment: Black and white with strong contrast and visible grain. A single red or white title card may break the grey.
grade_recipe: Print black and white with a contrast of +10% to +20%.
Keep the blacks at 3% or higher so that the grain shows.
Let archive clips keep their own grey, scratches and dirt.
Use red for a title card or a flag only, in less than 5% of the film.
Do not add a LUT or a soft glow.
colour_and_grade.texture: Coarse 16mm grain, scratches on the archive clips and a clipped sky

editing_and_rhythm.average_shot_length: 3 to 8 s (estimate; check Cinemetrics for each title)
editing_and_rhythm.shot_length_range: 1 s for an archive flash to 3 min for a speech
editing_and_rhythm.cutting_logic: Cut on the claim: an image meets a slogan, a number or a clip from the news, and the clash makes the point.
editing_and_rhythm.transitions: Hard cut and a cut to black between chapters; no dissolve.
editing_and_rhythm.runtime: 60 to 270 min, in chapters (estimate; the long form is for a debate)

sound.approach: Mixed sound: sync speech on location, a voice-over, a song and the noise of a crowd.
sound.dialogue: Direct speech to the camera, interviews and slogans; people interrupt and overlap.
sound.music: Folk songs and drums from the people in the film; a short piece of archive sound.
sound.loudness: −18 LUFS integrated, with a wide range

titles_and_graphics.treatment: Plain slogan cards, chapter titles, dates and figures; a hand-lettered or typed text on black or on a poster.
titles_and_graphics.type: A heavy sans-serif or a typewriter face in white on black, 2 to 5 s per card.

shot_primer.opening: Open on a street or a factory gate, with a slogan card over the first 5 s.

shot_list.shot: A worker speaks to the camera
An archive newsreel insert of dock workers at a port
A meeting in a union hall

positive: handheld camera in a crowded street

emotion.target_response: Urgent solidarity: the viewer sees a struggle as a fact and feels the call to take a side.

avoid_when: The brief needs a calm, neutral observer.
The brief needs a polished, glossy look.
The film must entertain and make no claim.

modifiers.how: Drop the slogans and the archive clips; keep the handheld 16mm and let the camera wait and listen.
Keep the political claim; build it from shorter shots, hard cuts of 1 to 3 s and clashes of image against image.

colour_temperature.note: The film is black and white; this sets the tint of a toned print only.

sources.title: Fernando Solanas and Octavio Getino, Toward a Third Cinema (Tricontinental, 1969)
